Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with a trip to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Nabizada stunner edges Watford past Southampton as ‘Spygate’ still looms large
Sports.content:
Southampton will have to get used to being barracked as they travel the Championship this autumn, the “Spygate” team set to be everyone’s favourite boo boys in the second tier. Certainly that was the case in Hertfordshire, with Watford fans and players alike beside themselves after a hard-fought victory, decided by two memorable first-half goals.

Tonda Eckert, the Southampton head coach, remains under investigation for his part in the Spygate affair and presented a subdued figure both during and after this contest. He insisted that his team were more united than ever after suffering the indignity of being removed from last season’s playoffs, “but it would be easier to say that after a victory”, Eckert acknowledged.

Watford paid tribute to Kenny Jackett before the match, the one-club legend and local boy hailed with two minutes of applause. This celebration of longevity and connection, with a Panini-inspired tifo tumbling down the stands, cut a contrast with the current operation, where Alessio Dionisi has become Watford’s 12th full-time manager in just the past five years.

“I am very tired and my team was too by the end,” said the Italian who was coaching Empoli in Serie B last season. Dionisi praised the attitude of his team – “I liked the mentality of my players, in every moment I saw one team working together,” he said. He also benefited from the Pozzo family’s multi-club network and the local academy in digging out a victory.

The Spain under-21 attacker Iker Bravo was one of several signings to make the familiar trek from “sister” club Udinese this summer, and he made his mark quickly, opening the scoring with a quite stunning solo goal in the 12th minute. It was all his own work and Bravo had to deploy a combination of skills to turn an innocuous situation into real danger. Looking to latch on to a long ball some 40 yards from goal, the 6ftplaymaker won the first header then, crucially, got a second touch with an outstretched toe to get the ball under control. Bravo then span immediately and drove at goal, pushing his way into the box before chopping right and getting off a low shot that Daniel Peretz got a hand to, butcould not keep out.

View image in fullscreen Watford’s Amin Nabizada jumps for joy after scoring their second goal against Southampton. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA

A great way to start any season, the energy among the Vicarage Road crowd grew immediately and the home side went on to dominate the first half. They doubled their lead in the 29th minute with a moment to remember for 19-year-old academy graduate Amin Nabizada who exploited the same gaps on the left of the Southampton defence to run with the ball from his own half before finishing precisely from a tight angle. “Nabizada was emotional but after the first 10 minutes he played well,” Dionisi said. “When there is one mentality amongst the team, then it’s better for him too.”

Southampton had the better of the second half, taking advantage of a drop in tempo from the hosts to assert their interests. A spell of concerted possession in the 56th minute ended with Kuryu Matsuki pulling out wide, the young midfielder Cam Bragg moving unmarked into the half space and his shift left finding the Canada World Cup star Cyle Larin to poke home from 10 yards out.

Larin had a chance to equalise just two minutes later with a shot on the turn but Federico Ravaglia – another new signing to impress for the Hornets – turned the ball round the post. When Finn Azaz came on as a second-half substitute for the Saints he bought an inch to fire off a low drive that went just beyond the left hand post. As a succession of dangerous set pieces were sent over by Ryan Manning, Southampton fans were singing “we’ll score when we want”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But as the game passed through a flurry of substitutions Eckert’s team were unable to generate enough momentum to truly unsettle Dionisi’s men. Their only further chance came in added time and was scuffed wide by Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Eckert said he had been happy enough with his team’s performance beyond “two errors in possession”. He insisted his squad are “very close and united” as a group. “We had a different expectation for the result but the group looks united and we now need to turn that into results.”

Opening matches rarely offer much insight into how a season will pan out. But Watford fans were able to enjoy both temperate weather and a decent performance. If Southampton want to transform the negative energy of Spygate into something positive, meanwhile, they will have to start again next week.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher reveals why Man United will NOT win the Premier League under Michael Carrick as Sky Sports pundit names the Spurs signing the Red Devils should have landed
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher reveals why Man United will NOT win the Premier League under Michael Carrick as Sky Sports pundit names the Spurs signing the Red Devils should have landed

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Michael Carrick lacks the 'stardust' to return Manchester United to the pinnacle of football, claims Jamie Carragher.

Carrick, 45, landed the Old Trafford gig on a permanent basis this summer having impressed during his interim stint in charge of the club following the sacking of Ruben Amorim in January.

The former United midfielder led the Red Devils to victories over Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool to deliver a third-place finish, returning the club to the Champions League after two seasons out of the competition.

Carrick's strong start to life in the United dugout has led to a groundswell of optimism among fans that he can oversee the club's first league title since Sir Alex Ferguson's departure in 2013.

However, Liverpool legend Carragher has urged caution ahead of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

'I'm not saying it's going to go wrong. What Manchester United have had for the last six months, need that for another 12 months of not being the circus, not being the story all the time, and Carrick brings you that,' he said on The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet.

Michael Carrick lacks the 'stardust' to deliver a Premier League or Champions League title for Manchester United, Jamie Carragher has claimed

Carrick has landed the United job on a permanent basis after an impressive interim spell

'But has he got that stardust to win the biggest trophy? And I think you need to get to a strong position of being a proper Champions League club again. And then, right, what do we need? It's like a player gets you to a certain level, then we need that stardust.

'I personally just don't think Michael Carrick's got that stardust as a manager to win a Champions League or a Premier League.

'I don't believe Michael Carrick will win the league or the Champions League with Manchester United, but he's done a really good job.

'He could have a good season and put Manchester United in a position to then go and get a Champions League-winning manager.'

Carrick has sought to strengthen his squad in the summer transfer market, with midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans arriving from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively.

But Carragher believes United missed a trick in not pursuing former West Ham star Mateus Fernandes, with the club baulking at his £85million asking price. The midfielder has since joined Spurs.

‘I was a little bit worried when I saw United linked with Fernandes because I thought that could be a good signing,’ he said.

‘I just looked at him and his age and was surprised United didn’t go for Fernandes. They said it was too expensive but was it that expensive?

Carragher believes Carrick can set a good foundation for the next Man United manager

He also questioned why the Red Devils pulled out of a move for £85m Mateus Fernandes

‘I know £85m is a lot but you’re never going to get a really top midfielder now for £50m.’

Elsewhere, United legend Paul Scholes believes the defence is 'still a problem', with United yet to bring in fresh additions at the back.

'Centre halves are still a problem,' he said. 'Manchester United still need better centre halves – the current players don't have the quality, where I am judging Manchester United, to go on and win the Premier League.

'You need centre halves who are reliable every single week. We've got Maguire who has started to pick up some [injury] niggles, Lisandro Martinez – the lad just can't stay fit now. When he's fit, he is a good player, don't get me wrong.

'They've got Leny Yoro who has struggled over the last two years – it looks like the [Premier League] level is above him and [hopefully] he might come on [a bit this season].'

Former Bayern Munich defender Matthijs de Ligt has been sidelined since November with a long-term back injury, with no clear sign as to when he will return.

Scholes believes the 27-year-old is the club's best defender – if he can stay fit.

'If de Ligt is fit and playing every week, he's possibly Manchester United's best centre-half. But again, that's a question mark against centre-halves. You can't have those question marks.'

Sports.title: Actress Hayden Panettiere dead at 36: Hollywood star known for roles in Heroes and Nashville remembered for bringing 'joy to all who knew her' after shock passing
Sports.content:
Actress Hayden Panettiere has been remembered as 'an incredible light and a force of nature' after her death at the age of 36.

The former child star, who was known for her roles on the hit NBC series Heroes and musical drama Nashville, leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter.

Representatives for Panettiere announced on Sunday: 'It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden.

'She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her - and to the millions who watched her onscreen.'

Her cause of death was not immediately clear. But law enforcement sources said that police responded to an incident involving the actress and that an investigation is ongoing.

'There's an investigation ongoing,' her representative added in a statement to NBC News. 'We should know more tomorrow.'

Sources also told TMZ that Panettiere had been recently complaining of back pain and that she and her on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, flew from Los Angeles to the south just one day before her tragic passing.

Beloved actress Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36. She leaves behind her daughter, who is 11. Panettiere is pictured here attending the Met Gala in 2014

Panettiere is seen on May 19, 2026 in New York City, promoting her new book. The tragic news comes just months after her memoir, This is Me, became a New York Times bestseller. The actress had become candid about her struggles dealing with fame, especially as a child star, in the months before her passing

Panettiere started out as a child star, with her first acting gig at just 11 months old

The Hollywood star earned multiple award nominations across her career, most notably while playing cheerleader Claire Bennet on Heroes and Juliette Barnes on Nashville.

Panettiere, who was set to turn 37 on Friday, also appeared in the Scream franchise as Kirby Reed, and lent her voice to the video games Until Dawn and Kingdom Hearts.

She is predeceased by her brother, Jensen, who passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart' at the age of 28.

Panettiere recently released a memoir

Panettiere said that she felt like she 'lost half of her soul' following his death, and revealed that the stress of his loss resulted in her body 'ballooning out', which left her in a 'really bad' and 'destructive' place.

The tragic news of her death comes just months after her memoir, This is Me: A Reckoning, became a New York Times bestseller. In the book, Panettiere described how she contended with fame and handled the difficulties in her life.

She had suffered from drug addiction, beginning when she was just 15 years old. At the time, she claimed she started taking 'happy pills' in an effort to make her seem more 'peppy' during interviews.

Her addiction then became worse while she was battling postpartum depression following the birth of her daughter Kaya in 2014.

But Panettiere has been sober in recent years, she said in a 2022 interview, noting that 'it's an everyday battle.'

Hayden Panettiere is pictured playing the character Claire Bennet in the NBC sci-fi drama series Heroes

The actress's younger brother, Jansen Panettiere, passed away in February 2023 from 'an enlarged heart'. They are seen together here in 2011

Hayden Panettiere has tragically died at the age of 36. Her cause of death was not immediately clear. The Hollywood star is pictured here at a gala in Hollywood in 2022

Panettiere leaves behind an 11-year-old daughter with ex, Wladimir Klitschko

'It's an everyday choice, and I'm checking in with myself all the time,' Panettiere told People at the time. 'But I'm just so grateful to be part of this world again, and I will never take it for granted again.'

Panettiere has also told how she nearly died during childbirth, and later relinquished custody of her daughte, who now lives in Europe, to her ex, former heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, while struggling with postpartum depression in 2018.

Speaking of the decision, Panettiere said she 'desperately' needed help at the time and insisted that Kaya does not feel 'abandoned' while appearing in a recent episode of the On Purpose with Jay Shetty podcast.

'The idea that anybody would think that I would just give away my child and be okay with it is heartbreaking. Couldn't be further from the truth,' the actress said.

'I was struggling with mental health and anxiety and postpartum and having to act my way through it, and just feeling like I completely lost myself,' she added.

Panettiere is remembered for her role as Claire Bennet on the hit NBC series Heroes

Panettiere is seen during her book tour in New York City in May

Panettiere is seen crying following her brother's celebration of life event in their hometown of Palisades, New York

Panettiere is pictured with her daughter, after telling how she almost died during childbirth

Panettiere has also come out as bisexual while she promoted her new book, telling Us Weekly in May: 'It's sad that I had to wait till I was 36 years old to share that part of me, but better late than never, right?

'I've chosen to share it with the world, I'm comfortable saying I'm bisexual. I'm comfortable to confidently say that, yes, I am bisexual. I said it!'

Despite having little privacy due to 'paparazzi always outside waiting for me,' Panettiere still managed to secretly date women, whom she preferred to men from 'a very, very young age.'

'[I was] much more into women,' the two-time Golden Globe nominee said. 'But, yeah, I have explored it, but I don't think I ever had the courage, because I hadn't shared this with anybody.

'I didn't really have the courage to throw myself fully, emotionally into it, because then if I did fall in love, that wasn't something that I wanted to ever have to hide. I didn't feel confident enough, and I was too afraid to really let that part of me explore that part of me.'

By the age of 19, Panettiere dissolved her business relationship with her mother, who was also her manager at the time.

Panettiere came out as bisexual as she promoted her new book. The actress is pictured here as Claire Bennet in Heroes

She played Juliette Barnes on the ABC show Nashville, releasing a number of her own songs

Panettiere is pictured with actor Adrian Pasdar on the set of Heroes

Panettiere was born on August 21, 1989 in Palisades, New York, and first started acting at just 11 months old, appearing in a commercial.

Her full-time acting career then began in 1994 when she played Sarah Roberts in the ABC soap opera One Life to Live until 1997. She then went on to play Lizzie Spaulding in the CBS soap opera Guiding Light from 1996 to 2000.

For her role on Pixar's A Bug's Life, she was nominated for a Young Artist Award and Grammy Award, making her the fifth-youngest nominee for a Grammy.

Her other credits include Remember the Titans, Ally McBeal, Racing Stripes, Ice Princess and I Love You, Beth Cooper.

But it was her role as a cheerleader with superpowers in Heroes, for which she won three Teen Choice Awards, that propelled her to fame in 2006, with the series revolving around the mantra: 'Save the cheerleader, save the world.'

Panettiere has also recorded a number of songs for the films and television programs she was in, including My Hero is You for the Disney Channel film Tiger Cruise and I Fly for the Disney film Ice Princess, which she co-starred in with the late Michelle Trachtenberg.

Panettiere has opened up about her struggles with addiction, beginning when she was just 15

Her first single not associated with an acting role, the reggae-infused Wake Up Call, was digitally released on August 5, 2008.

Clothing brand Candie's announced it was premiering an ad campaign for the single in late July of that year, and provided additional promotion for the song with a television ad and a music video starring Sebastian Stan, who played Panettiere's brother in The Architect.

Panettiere later played a brash country upstart opposite Connie Britton on Nashville, which aired on ABC for four seasons before being canceled and revived on CMT.

She did her own singing for the show, earning her some hits on the country charts as well as two supporting actress Golden Globe nominations.

In total, Panettiere had 11 songs recorded for Nashville appear on Billboard´s Hot Country Songs charts during the show's run, including two featuring Britton.

Following the news of her death, actor Randall Slavin shared a photo of him with Panettiere, writing: 'Peace be with you.'

She had shared the same photo just two weeks prior, with the caption, 'Good times and good friends.'

Actress Selma Blair also wrote on Instagram: 'I love you. Don't be gone. Don't be gone. Please,' while Melissa Barrera posted to her Instagram story: 'Rest in peace sweet Hayden.'

SAG-AFTRA added that it 'mourns the sudden passing of Hayden Panettiere.'

Sports.title: Britain's QUADRUPLE golden girl Amy Hunt eyes up 'eight-week hibernation' with her family after celebrating four European Championship gold medals with champagne
Sports.content:
Track hero Amy Hunt says she intends to 'hibernate for eight weeks' to celebrate her four gold medals at the European Championships in Birmingham.

But first Hunt, who once described herself as a 'track goddess', is getting straight back to work this week as she has a few weeks left of the Diamond League season.

The 24-year-old Cambridge University graduate toasted her haul with a glass of champagne on Sunday night alongside her coach Marco Airale.

Hunt claimed the 100m and 200m golds before being part of winning teams in the women's and mixed 4x100m relays.

She told Sky Sports News: ‘It’s important to celebrate the wins when they happen and live in the moment. You don’t win four golds often. I had a little glass of champagne with my coach last night. It’s straight back to work at the end of the week.

‘It's been euphoric. I’ve been living in dreamland this whole week, especially at home with great crowd support. I have such a pride in competing for Great Britain on a Great British stage. We really put the great in Great Britain.

Amy Hunt says she plans to hibernate for eight weeks at the end of the athletics season

The self-proclaimed 'track goddess' won four gold medals at the European Championships

‘I thought there was a chance. Any time you line up at a race, you have to believe you’ll win no matter what. It’s a very dog eat dog world so you have to have that confidence on the start line. I was lucky I got to cap off the relays with incredible people.'

'We were the sprint nation at this Championships. We cleaned up nearly every medal at the sprints. We're just so competitive and want it so badly. We hold our weight ona global stage - we go toe-to-toe with the Americans. It's great to see that programme come together.

'If you heard our coahces' team speeches, you'd want to go to war for them too. Our instructions for the relay were to go out there and break their hearts! It definitely fires you up and makes you ready to go.'

She added: 'My way of switching off is spending time with my family. I’m so lucky that I train out of Italy in Padova but I don’t get to see my family too often.

'Relaxing is spending time at home with my dog and sister, who just qualified as a nurse two days ago. I’ve got a few holidays booked. We've got a month left on the Diamond League Circuit - I've got the World Ultimate Championships in Budapest at the end of September.

'My coach gives us eight weeks off - he’s very benevolent. I have eight weeks of hibernation!’

Hunt picked up gold alongside Dina Asher-Smith, one of her heroes, in the women's 4x 100m relay.

Thanks to that triumph, Asher-Smith became the joint-most successful athlete in European Championships history. She has seven golds, two silvers, and a bronze.

Hunt, 24, said she 'wanted it all' at the start of the week - and she is going home with it!

Hunt added: 'Creating history together as two young women on a global stage is incredible. Who gets to do that?

'Dina is someone who I've looked up to my whole career. Not just the way she's amazingly quick and a world champion, but the way she handles herself and she was one of the first women to do a very academic degree and chase that life off the track and still be fabulous on the track. She's a role model.

'To help her become a big part of history is amazing.'

On now being a role model herself, she added: 'It’s crazy to me. I’ve been helped along my way by so many successful and amazing and gorgeous and fast women so to be in the same conversations is amazing.

'You can be soft and be strong, you can be great on the track and in the classroom, be a mother and have a successful career, have everything you’ve ever dreamed of.

'There's no world where you need to put limits on yourself. Anything you set your mind to you can achieve.'

The Cambridge University graduate's bubbly personality has endeared her to fans and brands alike, with sponsors reportedly queueing up to join forces with the 'relatable' star.

Her Instagram page, followed by 142,000 people, showcases her love of culture and literature as well as her exploits on the track, which have hit new heights since her breakthrough World Championship 200m gold in Tokyo last year.

She was not shy when broadcasting her aim to become the fastest woman in Europe, channelling her love of High School Musical when stating 'I want it all' at the start of the week.

The Newark athlete, who went to the same school in Grantham as Margaret Thatcher, has only bolstered her reputation with her feats.

Sports.title: Serie A footballer airlifted to hospital and in intensive care after he almost drowned in a swimming pool at a Sardinian mansion
Sports.content:
Serie A footballer airlifted to hospital and in intensive care after he almost drowned in a swimming pool at a Sardinian mansion

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A Serie A striker is in intensive care after being airlifted to hospital when he almost drowned in a swimming pool at a mansion in Sardinia, Italy.

Top-flight club Cagliari are reported to be 'worried' after 20-year-old French forward Yael Trepy had to be transported to hospital by helicopter following the incident on a day off after their Italian Cup match on Friday.

Reports from Sardinian newspaper Unione Sarda this morning read: 'The accident occurred during the afternoon, when the young striker lost consciousness.' It continued that at hospital 'Trepy performed all the necessary tests, which fortunately were negative.'

Italian national newspaper La Repubblica say Trepy cannot swim and ended up at the deep end of the swimming pool at a mansion in the luxury Costa Smeralda area.

In a statement released this morning Cagliari said: 'Cagliari Calcio announces that the player Yael Trepy is currently hospitalised at the Santissima Annunziata Civil Hospital in Sassari, where he is in intensive care.

Yael Trepy, pictured playing for Cagliari on Friday, is now in intensive care in hospital

Trepy is pictured at a swimming pool while on holiday from Cagliari duty last season

'The Club is in constant contact with the healthcare facility and the player's family and is closely monitoring the progress of his condition. At this time, Cagliari Calcio's thoughts are with Yael and his family. The Club also requests the utmost respect for their privacy and will provide any updates when available.'

Trepy, who scored once in eight appearances in his Serie A debut campaign last season, started Friday's game against Arezzo, playing 54 minutes.

Sardinia-based Cagliari brought Trepy into their youth academy system in 2022 and he has risen to play in their first team. He won the Italian equivalent of the FA Youth Cup in 2025, scoring in the final against AC Milan.

Cagliari's players were given two days off after beating Arezzo 1-0 and are due to resume training today. Their league season kicks off against Parma on Saturday.

They finished 14th in Serie A last season.

Sports.title: Novak Djokovic hints at mystery health concern as tennis star, 39, suffers in Cincinnati humidity in shock defeat by rank outsider Thiago Agustin Tirante
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic revealed he is battling a 'condition' after falling to his knees in apparent struggle during his shock defeat by Thiago Agustin Tirante.

The tennis great lost 2-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Saturday in a match that took two hours, 44 minutes in hot and humid conditions at the Cincinnati Open, and sparked concerns after the game.

'It's just a condition that I have, health-wise, that has been bothering me for the past couple of years,' Djokovic said after being questioned on his health. 'A lot of issues, especially when it is humid and it is hot.

'I did anticipate it (would be humid), but there are all these things, like nerves and everything involved that make it worse, and that's what happened.'

Djokovic, 39, appeared to struggle physically in the heat and had his 10-match winning streak in Cincinnati snapped.

He has had plenty of success in Cincinnati, with a 45-13 record and titles in 2018, 2020 and 2023. But he wasn't sure he would return.

Novak Djokovic falls to his knees during his R2 match in Cincinnati.



During the changeover, Novak appeared to be vomiting before receiving a medical timeout. #cincytennis pic.twitter.com/hHwxVQY5BB — Tennis Channel (@TennisChannel) August 15, 2026

Novak Djokovic hinted at an unknown health condition follow his defeat at the Cincinnati Open

The tennis great admitted he is unsure if he will ever return to the tournament after the loss

'I certainly hope so, but it looks more likely not, unfortunately,' Djokovic said. 'But let's see what the future brings.'

A 25-year-old from Argentina, Tirante is ranked No50 in the world. Djokovic – a three-time Cincinnati champion and No5 in the rankings – was playing for the first time since his loss to top-ranked Jannik Sinner in the semifinals at Wimbledon.

Up next for Djokovic is the US Open, which starts August 30 in New York.

Djokovic saved 13 of the 15 break points he faced. Tirante broke Djokovic's serve in the ninth game of the final set and then served it out.

'I think this is the best win of my career,' Tirante said. 'I think I really did a good job inside the court. I managed very well the nerves of playing against a legend like Novak.'

In a rain-delayed match that ended at 2.15am Sunday, top-seeded Alexander Zverev rallied to avoid a third straight loss, beating Cameron Norrie 3-6, 6-3, 6-3. After losing to Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon final, Zverev – the French Open champion – returned to play in Montreal and fell to Tallon Griekspoor in his opener Aug. 5.

On the women's side, Alexandra Eala of the Philippines continued her run of strong play with a victory over Elena-Gabriela Ruse, who lost the first set and stopped playing in the second with an ankle injury. Eala – who is No20 in the rankings - won her first WTA singles title in Washington earlier this month and has won eight of her last nine matches.

American Jessica Pegula beat Simona Waltert 6-3, 6-2, improving her record to 25-6 on hard courts in 2026. The third-ranked Pegula won the title in Cincinnati in 2024.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon praised by Barcelona fans as England winger enjoys 'electric' first friendly appearance since £70m deal to replace Marcus Rashford
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon was lauded as the 'best player on the pitch' as the England winger made his first appearance for Barcelona since completing a £70m transfer.

Barcelona had moved quickly at the end of last season to sign Gordon from Newcastle, with the surprise move completed at the end of May ahead of the World Cup.

The Spanish giants have been forced to wait to see Gordon feature following England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, with his post-tournament break leading to the 25-year-old starting his pre-season late.

Gordon, however, was quick to make an impression as he featured for the first time in a friendly against Basel.

In the opening minutes, Gordon showed his pace as he dribbled past his marker at speed, before firing in a dangerous low cross that neither Eric Garcia nor Raphinha were able to finish.

Operating on the left of Barcelona's attack, Gordon made several darting dribbles and looked to provide crosses from the byline.

Anthony Gordon made his first appearance in a Barcelona shirt in their friendly against Basel

The £70m summer signing from Newcastle caught the eye during the first half of the match

Gordon's eye-catching start was nearly capped with a solo goal, with the winger picking the ball up midway through the Basel half and driving goalwards.

The England star forced a slip from the defending full back, before cutting onto his right foot and firing narrowly over the bar.

Barcelona based newspaper Sport declared Gordon had been the Catalans’ ‘best player in attack’ after his ‘very, very active’ appearance.

Another journalist summarised: 'Great minutes from Gordon in the friendly match between Barça and Basel.

'The Englishman is increasingly shaking off his marker and has delivered some fine crosses into the box.'

Gordon ultimately only featured in the first half for Barcelona as he works his way back to full fitness in pre-season.

AS reported that Gordon has already convinced Barcelona boss Hansi Flick to give him a starting role despite having only been in training for the past week.

Barcelona fans, however, appeared impressed with Gordon's performance and were optimistic about his role ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi was on target in Barcelona's 5-2 victory over Basel

'Gordon is such a breath of fresh air. He looks so electric and who needed zero adaption. Looking forward to him,' one said.

'Barcelona finally has a left winger that takes on defenders one on one Anthony Gordon. What a diamond,' another said.

A third wrote: 'Gordon will provide something that Barca has been lacking in recent seasons, a threat on the outside on the left. Also allows us to push the left sided midfielder higher and between the lines.'

LaLiga champions Barcelona had moved for Gordon at the start of the summer, with the club opting against signing fellow England international Marcus Rashford permanently after his loan spell last season.

Gordon had already impressed fans by speaking fluent Spanish at his unveiling, having revealed it had been a childhood dream to play for the Catalan side.

Barcelona earned a 5-2 victory in the friendly with fellow new signing Karim Adeyemi having opened the scoring in the first half.

Hamza Abdelkarim, Lamine Yamal and a brace from Jesse Bisiwu sealed Barcelona's victory.

Sports.title: Arsenal look ready to dominate English football with the rest of the top teams in transition. And one player has been transformed by being a champion, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Arsenal look ready to dominate English football with the rest of the top teams in transition. And one player has been transformed by being a champion, writes ISAAN KHAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Until a team has finally crossed the finish line, there are always niggling doubts.

The psychological scars Manchester City had meted out on Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal over a period of three years were debilitating for this club.

It went beyond the ‘Second again, ole, ole’ chants or bottler jibes. It created a feeling that the men in blue were always just around the corner, waiting for the Gunners to slip up.

That imagery has been flung out the window. There is a confidence flowing through them after last season’s Premier League triumph and it augurs well for their upcoming campaign, which begins against Coventry at the Emirates on Friday night.

Arsenal just didn’t let up against City. When one goal came, the hunger for another superseded any thoughts to protect their lead.

In times before, going ahead so early on - 24 seconds into the game - caused the Gunners to panic or retreat.

Arsenal attacked Manchester City ravenously and served vengeance for years of coming second to Pep Guardiola

This is a different team, though, one emboldened to seize the moment of being on top, with the chance to be dominant in the months ahead. The rest of the 'Big Six' are going through transitions, remember.

Martin Odegaard typified this spirit the most. Having endured a stop-and-start season plagued by various injuries including to his knee and shoulder, the Norwegian hounded the opposition, desperate to make up for lost time.

Odegaard glided with a swagger which hasn’t always characterised him, transformed from becoming a champion.

He also played a number of incisive through-balls, constantly looking to pierce the opposition backline.

It wasn’t just his play. He pressed hard, not giving the forwards an inch on the ball. His goal on 48 minutes topped the display as he dumbfounded Josko Gvardiol and Gianluigi Donnarumma with just three touches.

It’s been some time before the midfielder has played in such a commanding manner, leading from the front in a real captain’s display.

When he’s confident and fully fit, Odegaard is a tricky player to face. He also sets the temperature in an Arteta team in sync around his intricacies. They rely on his pressing and ability to create chances in congested areas.

The calls for Declan Rice to take on the armband have festered in the background but here reflected just why Arteta has stuck with Odegaard.

Martin Odegaard played with more swagger now that he is a champion and was constantly forward-thinking

Arteta warned afterwards: ‘Well, he missed five or six months for different things (last season) and it was extremely difficult for him to get any momentum. If we can maintain him fit, available with the players around him, we're going to see a very different Martin.

‘I sensed from the first day he joined that he has something else in the belly that he wants to prove and show, because the team needs it as well.’

The substitutions sent a message, too. Having knocked the opposition off the park, Arteta brought on Declan Rice for the second half, and Bukayo Saka along with Piero Hincapie on 60 minutes.

There’s a depth to Arsenal which makes them an uncomfortable prospect to face when they’re on song.

The message is clear: the Gunners are firing and eyeing further silverware in the distance.

Gunners' new flying winger

The attention given to Arsenal’s pursuit of a marquee left winger had somewhat let £34million Christos Tzolis go slightly under the radar.

He was earmarked as a squad player, an attacker who would be knocking on the first XI door in seasons to come.

The 24-year-old, brought in to replace Leandro Trossard, already looks like a smart piece of business on the left side of Arsenal’s attack.

His headed assist for Kai Havertz after peeling away from a defender, or accurate pass to set Odegaard on the way to scoring, reflected why the Gunners brought him in.

He’s there to impact play, targeting goals and assists in a team without a 25 goal-a-season striker.

It’s now six goal contributions in six pre-season games for Tzolis. The Greek isn’t here to settle for a spot on the bench.

Christos Tzolis looked right at home against Manchester City, providing two assists

There is an opportunity to stake his claim - even more so if a pricey winger isn’t signed before the end of the window.

Thus far, he hasn’t put a foot wrong.

A telling trio of absentees

The Arsenal squad omissions presented an extra sub-plot.

Those left out included Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus.

Nwaneri has been the subject of interest from various clubs. So, too, has Martinelli, the subject of a £38million bid from Galatasaray. Jesus is edging towards a move to Napoli.

Of the three, Jesus is the closest to the exit door. Arteta played down the omissions, saying: ‘There's nothing to do with that (leaving the club). It's just a fact that we can bring 18 outfield players and we believe that for today's game, these were the options that we needed, especially with the physical condition of certain players.’

The players that Mikel Arteta left out ar potentially telling for the upcoming campaign

He added to TNT Sports: 'It's really sad to not have the availability (for them). I've been fighting with the Premier League to get more in the squad. Hopefully we can change that rule so players can be part of the squad. They're very important for us.'

All the same, their omissions pointed in a particular direction.

Sports.title: Man Utd 'living in the past' as transfer failings exposed in damning Liverpool comparison
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'living in the past' as transfer failings exposed in damning Liverpool comparison

Manchester United's summer transfer business is under the microscope with several of their targets choosing to move to other Premier League sides

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is still seeking more signings before the summer is out

Manchester United have been accused of "living in the past too much" with major names now preferring moves to the likes of rivals Liverpool and Manchester City.

‌



The Red Devils have found it difficult to secure headline names in the transfer market with Michael Carrick preparing for his first full season. The club have made midfield additions a priority this summer, but have missed out on some of the players they've been linked with.

‌



Elliot Anderson made a £116million move to City having been linked with United, but ultimately decided that the blue half of Manchester was a better fit. Sandro Tonali was another name reportedly on the United radar, but he made a club-record £100m switch to Tottenham.

‌



So far Carrick has seen Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos arrive at Old Trafford, but more was expected of United this summer. Ruud Gullit believes top players want to join other clubs in England with the Red Devils struggling to evolve as their league title drought extends to 13 years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He told NY Sports Day: "Manchester United sometimes live in the past too much. You have to adapt to modern developments. Since Sir Alex Ferguson left, football has evolved rapidly. Clubs like Liverpool and Manchester City adapted far better to modern tactical interpretations. That’s why top players wanted to join those coaches and stay there, whereas United struggled to attract the very best talent."

‌



Mateus Fernandes was another player linked with a move to Manchester, but the midfielder ultimately moved to Tottenham for £85m. Real Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni was another on their radar, but the Old Trafford hierarchy have also been criticised for their refusal to challenge their rivals when it comes to transfer fees.

United were able to bolster their forward line this time 12 months ago with the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko all joining. That trio helped the club blossom in the second half of the season as Carrick led them to a third place finish - and a Champions League return.

View 2 Images Elliot Anderson chose Man City over Man Utd this summer

‌



That was done with the club having no European football and going out of both cup competitions at the first hurdle - meaning they played just 40 times all season.

This year Carrick will have to attempt to compete across four fronts, putting a greater strain on the squad's resources. As a result new arrivals were a must and the club are still eyeing up reinforcements at left-back and in attack, especially with some players potentially leaving Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's new life in Spain with fresh challenge at historic club
Sports.content:
Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has unfinished business in La Liga. The former Arsenal and Chelsea striker scored 11 goals in half a season at Barcelona to help them climb from ninth to second, but left after just 18 league appearances.

So, when the opportunity came to return to Spain's top flight with Deportivo A Coruna, he wasn't going to say no. The Galician club are back in La Liga for the first time since their 2018 relegation and the addition of the Gabonese striker sends a message.

"The passion is still there, definitely, otherwise I'd choose another challenge," Aubameyang told Mirror Football. "I had a few offers, but the passion is still there and I still want to challenge myself and think this one is a special challenge to try to bring back the club to its best.

"Next year is going to be 20 years since I started my career as a professional and I have to say the truth, I'm feeling quite good. I can still give a lot for the game and still have the passion, I think this will never change.

‌



"As long as my body says I can go, I will go. Obviously, if I feel one day I cannot give my best to play at the best level, I'll say maybe I stop, but for the moment I'm sure that I have some more years to give. This is why I accepted the challenge here, because I know I can really help, I can still score some goals, I can give some assists, I can be effective in the game."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Mikel Arteta 'fighting' to change Premier League rule that would suit Arsenal READ MORE :

The 2021/22 season was a tough one for Barcelona. Ronald Koeman was sacked in October with the Catalan club at risk of missing out on Champions League qualification, but the appointment of Xavi and the mid-season additions of Aubameyang and Ferran Torres helped them recover.

"I was happy to be part of this Barca team, even if at that time they were struggling," Aubameyang added. "We could reach second place. When I arrived, we were ninth and I think this was a big effort from the whole team.

‌



"I saw some guys saying I'm the hero of Barca, this is funny, but let's say I was happy to be at the club at this moment, I was happy to give some good moments and some good memories for the fans.

"I still have some good messages from the fans and think it was a really nice moment playing in Barca that I will never forget. But now I'm happy to be back, it's definitely a different situation but an exciting one and hopefully it's going to be a nice year ahead."

Aubameyang, now 37, has two sons with his wife Alysha. The last few years have brought upheaval with his club football - he has played for a different club every year since 2021, albeit with two separate years at Marseille - and now has responsibility as a leader on the pitch as he aims to use his experience to benefit team-mates new to the challenges brought by Spain's top flight.

Depor became just the ninth different team to win La Liga when they claimed the title in 1999/2000. The 26 years since have seen the title shared between just four sides - all repeat champions - so that precious triumph emphasises their status as one of Spanish football's historic clubs.

Aubameyang is under no illusions about where they stand these days, though. It's likely to take a while for them to climb back into the upper reaches of the table and the first task this season is survival.

"Obviously, I saw Deportivo back in the day in top form, playing [in the] Champions League," he said. "I think everyone likes Deportivo because they had a great time, winning La Liga, playing in the Champions League, so I'm happy the club is back in La Liga and I will try to give my best. It's a process, we're going to go step by step, but I want to live this history and give my best to leave my mark."

‌



4 View 4 Images Aubameyang's wife and sons joined him in England after he first moved to the Premier League with Arsenal (Image: David M. Benett/Dave Benett/Getty Images for Formula 1) 4 View 4 Images Aubameyang joins a long line of African talents at Depor including title-winning goalkeeper Jacques Songo'o (Image: AllsportUK /Allsport)

The club also has a rich history of African players. Cameroon goalkeeper Jacques Songo'o and Moroccan centre-back Noureddine Naybet were part of Depor's title-winning squad and Aubameyang now has a chance to add his own name to that iconic list.

"It's a lways a good thing to be representing Africa all around the world and especially here at this club," he said. "Hopefully we can mark our history by giving our best, giving my best, to bring the club back to where it belongs."

‌



At the same time, he recognises his role will involve work off the pitch as well as on it. There are a number of younger and less experienced players in Depor's squad and he has a role to play when it comes to showing them the ropes at the highest level.

"We know back in the day the club was playing [in the] Champions League and I think the club is doing the best to be back at the best level," he said. "Obviously, it's a process; we have to do it step by step, but I want to be part of this history.

"We have a good mix now because we have a lot of young talents and obviously they called me because I can bring my experience, my voice, and I can help on the pitch and off the pitch. This is going to be my role at the club. I'm happy to play this role and hopefully it can work."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola singles out three Liverpool stars as boss addresses problem area
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola singles out three Liverpool stars as boss addresses problem area

Liverpool defeated Como 2-0 in their final pre-season match on Sunday and Andoni Iraola was particularly impressed with the new-look defence, who provided a much-needed boost

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola got a morale-boosting win over Como (Image: Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola hailed his new-look defence after they provided a much-needed boost in a 2-0 pre-season win over Como on Sunday.

‌



Goals from Cody Gakpo and Jeremy Jacquet ensured the Reds went into their first Premier League game of the season with renewed confidence. Liverpool endured a tricky tour of the United States, with new boss Iraola desperately short of defenders.

‌



Iraola was forced to field Ifeanyi Ndukwe, 18, Luke Chambers, 22, and Mor Talla Ndiaye, 18, in pre-season, with Virgil van Dijk given a break after the World Cup, Joe Gomez ruled out early on, Jacquet not ready after injury and Giovanni Leoni also still rehabilitating from a long-term knee injury.

‌



With Ibrahima Konate released on a free transfer at the end of last season, there is a place up for grabs alongside Van Dijk in central defence for the 2026/27 campaign. With Gomez and Leoni fighting to get fit, it is a race between Jacquet - a £55million signing from Rennes - and Ronald Araujo, a loan signing from Barcelona.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Jacquet got the nod from the start against Como and got on the score sheet with a tap-in before being replaced by Araujo at half-time. Both players took the opportunity to catch Iraola's eye, along with right-back Jeremie Frimpong.

Asked if he was impressed by his two new centre-backs, Iraola replied: "Yes, both of them. I think Jeremy played really well. Also Ronald played really well when he came in. When you have two new faces, first game for both, they do so well.

"It was also a very good performance of Jeremie Frimpong, playing 90 minutes as a right-back, helping us offensively but closing very well his side also. So, some good performances at the back."

‌



View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet enjoyed a perfect Liverpool debut (Image: Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

The win over Como came after a 4-2 defeat by Leeds and a 3-2 loss against Monaco in pre-season. Iraola has been vocal in his frustration at the lack of incoming players in the summer transfer window, with defence and wide areas obviously short.

"I think we need a little bit this feeling of finishing with a clean sheet, winning the game," he added. "Still, the first half has been better than the second, but at least we kept our organisation, our composure and we found a way to finish with a clean sheet, 2-0. I think we needed this feeling before we start."

Liverpool begin their 2026/27 campaign against Newcastle at St James' Park on Sunday with some unanswered questions over their squad. The Reds are still chasing an elite attacker, with a move for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola still on the cards.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Barcola alternative sends message to Iraola as transfer plan clarified
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Barcola alternative sends message to Iraola as transfer plan clarified

Liverpool begin their Premier League campaign against Newcastle United in six days but their hunt for a new winger continues

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has less than a week until his first Premier League game as Liverpool boss (Image: Getty)

Liverpool now have less than a week until their Premier League campaign begins. But Andoni Iraola's side have only welcomed in three senior signings so far.

‌



This summer has been a relatively quiet one for the Reds. With the Iraola era underway, filling the void left by Ibrahima Konate's free transfer to Real Madrid has led the club to recruit two new centre-backs.

‌



Jeremy Jacquet has arrived from Rennes for £60million following negotiations in January and Ronald Araujo will likely partner Virgil van Dijk to begin the season after he signed on a one-year loan deal from Barcelona. The Uruguayan can be bought after his loan spell for £47.1m.

‌



Bradley Barcola has emerged as Liverpool's top target as they look to bolster their attacking arsenal, but their third summer addition, Victor Munoz, could ease any concerns. Mirror Football has a look at the latest updates out of Anfield.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool learn new PSG decision on Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye after transfer announcement READ MORE :

Liverpool finally change transfer stance after breakthrough in negotiations READ MORE :

Victor Munoz sends a message

The tail end of this transfer window appears set to be dominated by Liverpool's pursuit of Barcola. With Mohamed Salah now playing for Trabzonspor, a new superstar winger has been sought out and the Frenchman fits the bill.

‌



View 3 Images Munoz was the best player on the pitch for the Reds (Image: Getty)

However, as things stand, PSG's £130m asking price is out of Liverpool's price range. Not to mention, Barcola primarily plays off the left, whereas a right-winger is what the Reds really desire.

Munoz might have something to say about this, though. He has proved he can play a big role under Iraola. Liverpool faced Italian side Como twice on Sunday, with the first friendly taking place behind closed doors at AXA Training Centre. Munoz was the star of the show.

‌



The World Cup winner, who was signed from Osasuna for £34.6m in June, started on the left wing and was a danger from minute one. He tore Como right-back Ivan Smolcic to shreds and was taken off in the 46th minute of what was only a 70-minute match.

Munoz was so impressive that Iraola may need to reassess whether a player like Barcola is necessary. The French star likes it off the left and with Rio Ngumoha saying he's getting used to playing on both flanks, an alternative may already be at the club in the form of Munoz.

‌



Curtis Jones transfer plan

Munoz's team-mate Curtis Jones seems set to leave Liverpool this summer. He has been a target for Inter Milan for some time now, with Iraola preferring other options in the middle of the park.

Liverpool's £34m demand has so far proved too pricey for Inter, who have shifted midfield star Davide Frattesi to Lazio to free up wages and space.

View 3 Images Jones' future is uncertain (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

But now, reports in Italy suggest another midfielder will soon be sold, finally enabling them to scoop up Jones. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Luis Henrique, formerly of Marseille, is now on the chopping block.

When he is sold, Inter will move for the Liverpool midfielder. It is claimed that Roma are one of the few clubs interested in talking Henrique off Inter's hands.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Victor Osimhen statement made as Mikel Arteta drops next transfer clue
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Victor Osimhen statement made as Mikel Arteta drops next transfer clue

Galatasaray's stance on selling Victor Osimhen to Arsenal emerges

View 3 Images Galatasaray have addressed Victor Osimhen's future (Image: Getty Images)

The start of Arsenal's Premier League title defence is fast approaching, with the Gunners looking to get more business done before the big kick-off against Coventry. The Gunners have signed Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier so far, while Piero Hincapie's loan has become permanent.

‌



Arsenal's striker search has moved on to Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen, with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus potentially on their way out of the club before the end of the transfer window. Ethan Nwaneri and Martin Zubimendi could also depart before the September 1 deadline.

‌



Meanwhile, Jarell Quansah and Ezri Konsa have emerged as defensive targets as the Gunners wrestle with the absence of the injured William Saliba. The Gunners have seen at least one bid for Aston Villa's Konsa knocked back.

‌



Following Sunday's Community Shield final against Manchester City, Mirror Football brings you a round-up of the latest Arsenal transfer news…

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Osimhen statement made

Galatasaray have issued a strong 'hands off' warning amid Arsenal's interest in Osimhen. According to reports in Turkey, president Dursun Ozbek has told his inner circle: "I will not say 'yes' to any transaction that will harm Galatasaray or not benefit Galatasaray.

‌



Mikel Arteta sends clear transfer message to three Arsenal stars ahead of Community Shield READ MORE :

"What I said about Baris Alper Yilmaz, I am now saying even more strongly about Osimhen. No matter how much the price is, I am not selling Osimhen."

Despite Ozbek's declaration, Turkish outlet Sozcu reports that Arsenal remain 'determined' to sign the Nigerian, who has also responded to the speculation over his future, saying: "There are always rumours during the transfer windows. I'll focus on my job. I'm focused on my work. We'll see and think about what comes next then."

View 3 Images Arsenal remain keen on Osimhen (Image: Photo by Burak Basturk / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Arteta drops transfer clue

Mikel Arteta has dropped a clear hint that Nwaneri will soon be leaving the club. After being involved in pre-season, the attacking midfielder was omitted from the squad for Sunday's Community Shield against Manchester City.

Nwaneri's lack of involvement suggests he will be moved on before the end of the transfer window, with Galatasaray among the clubs interested in the youngster.

View 3 Images Ethan Nwaneri was in Cardiff but didn't make the squad (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Arteta addressed Nwaneri's future ahead of the Community Shield, saying: "I want him to be at the club but something is in the medium-long term what is best for the player as well. Ethan needs to play football and if he stays here it's because we can guarantee that he can have those minutes."

Arteta's selection for the first competitive match of the season suggests those minutes cannot be guaranteed.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt makes European Championships history as Team GB star caps off stunning week
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt makes European Championships history as Team GB star caps off stunning week

Amy Hunt had enjoyed a spectacular European Athletics Championship, but the Team GB ace had the opportunity to make history in Birmingham

View 3 Images Team GB set a new European Athletics record in the 4x100m mixed relay (Image: AP Photo/Matthias Schrader)

Amy Hunt secured her fourth European Athletics Championship gold medal winning the 4x100m mixed relay alongside Jeremiah Azu, Dina Asher-Smith and Zharnel Hughes.

‌



Germany took the silver while Spain had to settle for the bronze medal. Another golden evening for Team GB saw Hunt, Azu, Asher-Smith and Hughes cross the line within 39.95 seconds - a new European record on a history making night for British athletics.

‌



The magnificent team victory saw Hunt secure a historic quadruple golden triumph in Birmingham and become one of the country's biggest athletics stars. Coming into the mixed-relay final, Hunt had already struck gold three times in the Midlands.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Immediately after securing her precious fourth, Hunt said: "Oh my gosh, I am over the moon and I think to finish it off with my best friends in sport you know.

"To do it all together is incredible. That was the first time we did that changeover an hour ago in warm-ups and look how smooth it was - such professionals!"

‌



Before the race, she was unstoppable, convincingly taking gold in the 100m, 200m and 4x100m women's relay, the latter in which she did so alongside Imani-Lara Lansiquot, Success Eduan and Asher-Smith.

View 3 Images It was more gold for Amy Hunt at the European Championships (Image: British Athletics via Getty Images)

After the women's relay, the latter became the joint-most successful athlete in European Athletic Championships history - the gold in the mixed competition moved her into a league of her own.

‌



Not long after securing the victory, Asher-Smith, who surpassed Sandra Elkasevic and Jakob Ingebrigsten's joint-record of seven European medals, said: "I was terrified, I am going to be completely frank with you.

"When that gun was going I was like 'Dina please relax, it's only going to go well for you'. When I gave the baton to someone else I was so happy. I can't lie! That is exactly how I feel, very unfiltered, I was just like 'get this out of my hand, bye!'

View 3 Images Dina Asher-Smith and Amy Hunt are Team GB's latest history makers (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Hunt's campaign this year is comparable with legendary Dutch sprinter Fanny Blankers-Koen, who won three golds and a silver at the 1950 European Championships - Hunt surpassed the record by winning gold in all four sprinting events.

After the triumph, Azu also hailed Team GB's sensational team, adding: "That is exactly what we set out to do before we came here. We are super strong in the sprints and we needed to showcase that for the British fans.

"Getting to run with the two best British athletes in history...Amy is on the rise, what she has done at these Championships is incredible. It is good to have your name next to some incredible athletes."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
