Mark Levine (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images) Jasmin Savoy Brown y Hayden Panettiere en una escena de 'Scream 6' de 2023. ©Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection / Cordon Press Escena del largometraje 'Amber Alert' de 2024, con Hayden Panettiere y Tyler James Williams. ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection / Cordon Press

Fue muy pronto cuando los padres de Panettiere decidieron iniciarla en el negocio: con apenas 11 meses, su madre empezó a presentarla como candidata para anuncios de televisión. Con poco más de cuatro años ya actuaba en telenovelas: a mediados de los noventa apareció en una treintena de capítulos de Sólo se vive una vez, y en casi 50 de The Guiding Light, sobre una familia de clase media del medio Oeste estadounidense. También fue Maddie en Ally McBeal y la voz de Kairi en el videojuego Kingdom Hearts, así como Gen en Soñando, soñando triunfé patinando, donde compartía escenas con la también fallecida Michelle Trachteberg. Pero fue su papel en Bichos, como la princesa Dot, el que la lanzó a la palestra, en 1996, así como el de la hija de Denzel Washington en Titanes: Hicieron historia, en 2000.

Y después llegó Héroes. La ficción sobre superhéroes corrientes la catapultó a la fama en una época en la que las series de televisión quizá no gozaban del prestigio cultural que se les da hoy, pero sí en la que llegaban a millones de personas de todo el mundo casi a la vez. Entre 2006 y 2010, de los 77 episodios de la serie, su personaje de la animadora de instituto Claire, que tenía poderes para regenerarse, apareció en 73. También gracias a su personaje de Juliette Barnes en las seis temporadas de Nashville, que retrataba las dificultades de unos cantantes de country en la célebre ciudad de Tennessee, mejoró su aceptación entre la crítica, y llegó a estar nominada, tanto en 2013 como en 2014, a los Globos de Oro, como mejor actriz de reparto por la miniserie.

Cuando la serie acabó, en 2018, Panettiere bajó el ritmo. Participó en la saga de Scream y en películas como Amber Alert o Sleepwalker, su último proyecto. Uno de sus palees más queridos fue el de Al cruzar el tigre, en 2004, donde compartió pantalla con su hermano.

Hayden Panettiere, en la entrega de los premios Critics' Choice Awards en Santa Mónica, California, en enero de 2016. Jordan Strauss (AP/LaPresse)

Fue precisamente durante el rodaje de Héroes cuando mantuvo un romance con su compañero de reparto Milo Ventimiglia (conocido por las series Las chicas Gilmore y This Is Us). Empezaron a salir en 2007, cuando él tenía 30 años y ella 18, en una relación que terminó en 2009. “El problema radicaba en que no podía anteponer el ‘te quiero’ al ‘te amo’, y en ese momento no me daba cuenta ni entendía por qué me incomodaba tanto”, explicaba recientemente en sus memorias. “Solo podía decir ‘te amo’ de forma casual. Siendo mayor, él era mucho más consciente de lo que eso significaba. Y eso decía mucho”.

Todo ello ha quedado relatado en This Is Me: A Reckoning (que podría traducirse como Esta soy yo: un ajuste de cuentas), la biografía que publicó a mediados del pasado mes de mayo y que se convirtieron en un enorme éxito de ventas. En ella relataba, también, sus problemas con el alcohol. “El problema no era sobre lo que estaba o no estaba mal en mi vida. La cuestión estaba en que tenía todo lo que había deseado, y todavía era infeliz. Tenía depresión postparto, y eso era una mierda”, rezaba uno de los fragmentos.

En ella narraba también cómo poco después de esa ruptura empezó una relación con el boxeador ucraniano Vladimir Klichkó. Juntos tuvieron una hija, Kaya, en 2014; ella habló públicamente sobre sus dificultades tras el nacimiento de la niña y de cómo había lidiado con una depresión posparto. Tras una década de idas y venidas, Panettiere y Klichkó decidieron separarse en 2018: cuando estaban a punto de casarse, él canceló la boda por sorpresa, y después regresó, arrepentido, pero ella decidió no volver con él. En 2018, Panettiere abandonó su lucha por la custodia de la niña y se la dio a Klichkó, al que califica de “padre increíble”. “Siempre la he querido aquí, y siempre la echaré de menos”, afirmaba en el podcast de Shetty. “Siempre quiero tenerla entre mis brazos, pero mi vida no puede ser así ahora”. En las memorias, afirmaba: “No vivir bajo el mismo techo cada día ha sido la experiencia más dura de mi vida”.

Tras la separación, la actriz conoció a un hombre llamado Brian Hickerson, con el que afirmaba que había pasado por una de las etapas más complejas de su vida, que calificaba como “traumática”. En el año 2020, Hickerson fue acusado de cuatro delitos graves de violencia machista, así como de dos delitos graves de agresión con arma mortal y un delito grave de disuadir a una testigo, y también de otro delito menor de agresión. Tras declararse culpable de dos delitos graves de lesiones a Panettiere, fue condenado a cumplir 45 días en prisión. “Es un tema muy vergonzoso”, reflexionaba ella en ese libro publicado hace apenas tres meses. “Siempre me he considerado una mujer fuerte y resiliente. La idea de que pudiera permitir que me sucediera algo así me dejó atónita. A quienes mejor me conocían, también les dejó atónitos. Intenté mantenerlo en secreto, en la medida de lo posible, porque no quería involucrar a nadie a quien quisiera. Ya sabía que querían protegerme, y yo quería protegerlos, tanto física como emocionalmente. Fue humillante”.

En esa autobiografía, con la que se embarcó en una gira promocional por buena parte de Estados Unidos, también hablaba de su sexualidad y de cómo había escondido algunos aspectos de ella en su juventud. “Es algo de mí que nunca pude compartir con el mundo porque simplemente nunca fue el momento adecuado. Era demasiado joven y me obligaban a ser perfecta en todo momento, no me animaban a ser yo misma. Luego llegó la época en la que parecía que el hecho de que la gente, sobre todo las mujeres, se declarara ser bisexual o que le gustaran las chicas, era una moda pasajera. Tenía miedo de que, si era sincera, me acusaran de subirme al carro. Era un tema difícil de abordar con claridad”, contaba en un adelanto concendido a la revista Us Weekly. “He decidido compartirlo con el mundo, me siento cómoda diciendo con seguridad que sí, soy bisexual. ¡Lo dije! Esta es la primera vez que lo digo en alto”.

La promoción de This Is Me, publicado el 19 de mayo, le había traído alegría y un retorno de su popularidad. Había paseado por redacciones y platós de televisión, y era muy activa en redes sociales —su cuenta de Instagram acumula 1,1 millones de seguidores—. Tras narrar en el libro episodios difíciles de abuso de sustancias, depresión, ansiedad, paso por rehabilitación (durante ocho meses) y dismorfia corporal y explicar su mala relación con su madre o cómo se había enterado de la muerte de su hermano por teléfono, se sentía liberada. Como le dijo al diario The New York Times en una entrevista: “No me puedo creer que haya podido salir viva de todo esto”.

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo y Georgina Rodríguez comparten los secretos de su boda en una exclusiva: ceremonia en su sala de estar y misa posterior en Fátima
World.content:
El futbolista y la ‘influencer’ han abierto las puertas de su enlace a la revista ‘Vogue’, donde han explicado los motivos por los que han decidido invitar solo a sus cinco hijos y han confirmado que habrá una gran celebración en el futuro: “Algo íntimo es más inusual para nosotros”

Durante semanas, internet se plagó de rumores sobre la posible celebración de la boda de Cristiano Ronaldo (Funchal, 41 años) y Georgina Rodríguez (Buenos Aires, 32 años). Se especulaba sobre la fecha y el sitio, llegando, incluso, a movilizar el 8 de agosto a cientos de seguidores a un enlace en la catedral de Funchal que, al final, no era el de la famosa pareja. El futbolista y la influencer se casaron tres días después, el 11 de agosto, coincidiendo con el décimo aniversario de su primer encuentro en la tienda de Gucci de Madrid —donde ella trabajaba— y justo un año después de que ella hiciera público su compromiso a través de Instagram —entre los dos suman más de 750 millones de seguidores en esta red social—. El lugar escogido para la ceremonia tampoco ha sido una catedral, sino la sala de estar de su casa de verano en Cascais (Portugal). “Cuando era pequeña, soñaba con el castillo más grande, el carruaje más lujoso, el vestido más largo, una corona llena de diamantes. Y ahora digo: ‘No, quiero algo íntimo, con mi pareja y nuestros hijos, en casa’. Porque castillos, casas, islas, caballos, coches... todo eso lo tenemos al alcance de la mano cada día. Pero algo íntimo... eso es más inusual para nosotros”, ha reconocido Georgina a Vogue, que ha tenido acceso exclusivo a la íntima boda.

En contraste con las grandes bodas de este verano, como la de Dua Lipa con Callum Turner o la de Taylor Swift con Travis Kelce, que han contado con una lista de invitados llena de celebridades, el futbolista y la influencer han tenido solo cinco testigos en el momento de darse el “sí, quiero”: sus cinco hijos —Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., de 16 años (nacido antes de que se conocieran); los mellizos Mateo y Eva María, de nueve (nacidos en junio de 2017 por vientre de alquiler, una práctica ilegal en España, cuando ya estaban juntos); Alana Martina, de ocho años; y Bella Esmeralda, de cuatro—. En una de las fotografías del reportaje se ve a Georgina rodeada de los cinco, todos vestidos de blanco. “En el futuro tendremos una gran boda para poder celebrarla con familiares y amigos”, adelanta la también empresaria a Vogue.

La imagen de la portada digital de verano de Vogue muestra a los recién casados frente a la capilla de Nuestra Señora de los Dolores, en el Santuario de Fátima, a donde se trasladaron después de la ceremonia casera para celebrar una misa y recibir la bendición del sacerdote —Georgina ha hablado en más de una ocasión de su fe, tanto en sus redes como en su propio reality show—. Ella luce su majestuoso anillo de compromiso con un enorme diamante ovalado, que acompaña con unos pendientes a juego. “Hemos decidido hacerlo en el salón de nuestra casa, donde desayunamos, almorzamos y cenamos, y donde vivimos la realidad de nuestras vidas. Dentro de 30 años quiero que los niños piensen: ‘Algo maravilloso ocurrió en esta mesa: los votos matrimoniales de nuestros padres”, asegura la influencer. “Probablemente no será la misma mesa. Quizás cambiemos la decoración”, añade Cristiano a la revista de moda.

Ambos fueron vestidos de Gucci —igual que sus hijos—, en homenaje a aquel primer encuentro en el que saltó la chispa en la tienda de la marca en Madrid. Ella optó por un dos piezas de falda y pantalón, y unos zapatos de satén a juego con el característico detalle de la herradura plateada. Él, por su parte, lució un traje de algodón beige claro hecho a medida, igual que los mocasines. “Fue increíblemente especial vestir a Georgina y Cristiano para este momento, sabiendo que su historia de amor comenzó en una tienda Gucci de Madrid. Tiene algo muy romántico, un hermoso cierre de círculo, casi como un cuento de hadas moderno”, comenta Demna, director artístico de la marca, en declaraciones a la revista. “No quería que en un día tan sencillo para nosotros fuéramos vestidos de gala”, aporta Georgina sobre los looks.

En un momento de la entrevista, Cristiano recuerda ese primer encuentro: “Estaba de espaldas a ella y entonces me giré y la vi. Nuestras miradas se cruzaron y, a partir de ese momento fue...”. “Fue un sueño”, remata su ya mujer. “Sí, un sueño. Sé que ella es el amor de mi vida y creo que yo también lo soy. Creo que ella piensa que yo soy el amor de su vida”, señala el futbolista.

El álbum de fotos del enlace incluye varias imágenes de la pareja entrenando en su gimnasio personal, detalles de un rosario o del calzado que lucieron todos los miembros de la familia en la boda, así como varias instantáneas tomadas en el Santuario de Fátima. “Fue exactamente como lo había imaginado: íntima, llena de amor, y con nuestra familia como protagonista indiscutible. No pude contener las lágrimas”, reconoce Georgina. “No necesitaba nada más: a mi esposo, a mis hijos, nuestro hogar, nuestra fe y nuestro amor”, añade.

Y, según confirma la pareja, no habrá luna de miel, ya que al día siguiente tuvieron que regresar a su casa de Riad (Arabia Saudí) porque Cristiano comenzó los entrenamientos con su actual equipo, el Al-Nassr F. C., el pasado 15 de agosto. “Cada día es una luna de miel”, dice el futbolista.

World.title: Feyenoord and Ajax surrender two-goal leads as AZ top Eredivisie

AZ Alkmaar and Groningen share the lead in the Eredivisie after two rounds after two of the big three unexpectedly dropped points at the weekend.

AZ, who beat champions PSV 4-0 to win the Johan Cruyff Shield two weeks ago, continued their good form with a 4-1 win at Utrecht.

The first three goals came in a five-minute spell around half-time, with Peer Koopmeiners giving AZ the lead with a header from a corner just before the interval.

Weslley Patati charged down the right-hand touchline and scored from a narrow angle for the second before Mexx Meerdinck settled the contest in the 49th minute, with Ayoub Oufkir adding a late fourth.

Groningen won by the same scoreline at newly promoted ADO, taking the direct approach to go 3-0 up before half-time.

All three goals were set up by long balls from goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen, with Thom van Bergen opening the scoring with some neat footwork after 15 minutes.

Brynjólfur Willumsson and David van der Werff added to the scoreline in the first half before 21-year-old substitute Nils Eggens headed in a fourth nine minutes from the end.

Heerenveen hit back

Ajax and Feyenoord both surrendered two-goal leads at home to miss the chance to take an early lead in the title race.

Ajax looked to be cruising against Heerenveen when a superb strike in the 33rd minute by Abdellah Ouzane put them two up, following an own goal by Bernd Klaverboer.

But Jacob Trenskow pulled one back just before half-time and despite Ajax laying siege to the visitors’ goal, it was Heerenveen who had the last word when substitute Maxence Rivera found the net with a fierce shot in the 82nd minute.

Feyenoord suffered similar jitters after dominating the first half against Go Ahead Eagles, with goals from Gjivai Zechiël and last season’s top scorer Ayase Ueda putting them firmly in control.

But the Deventer club hit back through Søren Tengstedt and a header by Stefan Ingi Sigurdarson, the latter within minutes of coming on as a substitute. Both teams hit the crossbar in a frantic last nine minutes, but ultimately had to share the points.

PSV first win

PSV, who dropped points in their opening match against Fortuna Sittard, overcame Excelsior with an early goal by Ruben van Bommel and a tap-in by Ricardo Pepi from his USA international team-mate Sergino Dest’s pass.

Excelsior were briefly level early in the second half when Casper Widell headed in a teasing cross, but Peter Bosz’s side were much improved as new signing Kodai Sano came on after an hour.

NEC Nijmegen warmed up for their Champions League play-off contest in midweek with a 4-1 win against newcomers Willem II, with veterans Tjaronn Chery and Bryan Linssen among the scorers as well as summer signing Kaj Sierhuis.

All three promoted teams are still looking for their first point after Cambuur Leeuwarden lost 3-1 at Fortuna Sittard despite a battling second-half display.

Sparta denied Telstar a share of the early championship lead by winning 3-1 in IJmuiden, while Twente won the Overijssel derby by the same score with the help of an own goal by PEC Zwolle striker Dylan Mbayo.

World.title: Belgian demand pushes Dutch coal plants to run harder
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch coal-fired power stations have generated more electricity so far this year than in the whole of 2024, driven by high gas prices and a sharp rise in demand from Belgium, the Financieele Dagblad reported on Monday.

Coal plants normally run harder from October, when electricity demand rises and less wind and solar power is available.

The figures come from data platform Nationaal Energie Dashboard. Coal was last burned at this rate during the 2022 gas crisis, when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine pushed gas prices so high that coal became the cheaper fuel.

Belgian shortfall

Much of the extra output has left the country. Belgium took its last two working nuclear reactors offline, which went offline in April for safety upgrades.

That left Belgium importing 7.5 billion kWh more electricity than it exported in the second quarter, a record, beating a previous high set in late 2015. Most of it came from the Netherlands and France.

“Coal plants are also stepping in,” energy transition specialist Martien Visser at Hanze University of Applied Sciences in Groningen told broadcaster NOS, “because demand for electricity from abroad has increased.”

Climate trade-off

Visser said the extra Dutch emissions were not necessarily bad news, because European rules cap total emissions across member states, so higher output in one country can mean less elsewhere.

“Not all countries are moving at the same speed on the energy transition,” he told NOS, adding that Dutch coal was preferable to German lignite, which is dirtier. Burning coal also frees up gas – 60 million cubic metres a week, or around 20% of Dutch demand.

Coal is the most polluting way to generate electricity, and Dutch law requires the three remaining plants, two on the Maasvlakte near Rotterdam and one in the Eemshaven, to stop burning it by 2030.

CDA leader Henri Bontenbal called earlier this year for the plants to stay open as a backstop.

World.title: Dutch women win 4x400m relay for fifth European gold medal
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The women’s 4x400m relay team claimed the Netherlands’ fifth gold medal of the European athletics championships with a third successive victory in the event.

The Dutch drafted in Lieke Klaver, bronze medalliist in the individual 400m, and Femke Broeders-Bol, who won bronze at 800m, as they faced a strong challenge frorm the British team.

Myrte van der Schoot and Klaver built a commanding lead on the first two legs, but the British closed the gap on Eveline Saalberg on leg three to set up a showdown between Broeders-Bol and Emily Newnham.

Broeders-Bol held Newnham on her shoulder for the first 300m before pulling away in the home straight to finish half a second clear in an overall time of 3 minutes 21.1 seconds.

In the final event of the championships in Birmingham, the the men’s team added a bronze medal, their first ever in the 4x400m relay, in a photo finish with Belgium.

Jonas Phijffers, who also won bronze in the individual 400m, edged out Belgium’s Daniel Segers on the line by 0.02 seconds as the Dutch quarter of Eugene Omalla, Keenan Blake, Liemarvin Bonevacia and Phijffers finished in 2 minutes 59.49 seconds. Italy won the gold medal, just 0.03 seconds ahead of the British team.

Best ever haul

The two medals on the last day completed the Netherlands’ most successful ever performance at a European athletics championships, with 14 medals, five of them gold.

The Dutch finished fourth in the overall medal table behind Italy, who won nine gold medals, Great Britain and Germany.

Jessica Schilder won the women’s shot put with a commanding performance ahead of Jorinde van Klinken, who went on to take gold in the discus with her opening throw on Friday.

Nadine Visser won her first European outdoor title at 100m hurdles by the smallest possible margin of 0.001 seconds, while the biggest surprise was Stefan Nillessen’s victory in the men’s 1500m final on Saturday.

Broeders-Bol’s two medals made her the most successful Dutch athlete in the history of the European championships with eight medals – the same number as Fanny Blankers-Koen amassed in the 1950s.

However, Broeders-Bol, 26, won six gold medals, one more than Blankers-Koen, as well as a silver and a bronze, across three championships.

World.title: Rain returns this week but drought is far from over
World.content:
Rain is forecast across the Netherlands for most of this week, ending a long dry spell – but forecasters say it will do little to undo the drought that has left rivers at record lows. Rain will fall overnight into Tuesday and continue on Wednesday.

The fifth regional heatwave of the year has now ended, which matched a record set in 1947, with temperatures falling back to 19 to 22°.

From Thursday, showers are expected daily, some heavy and accompanied by thunder.

Little relief

The rain will ease the drought but not resolve it, forecasters said. The ground has baked so hard that water from brief showers barely sinks in, broadcaster NOS reported.

The Netherlands remains at level two of a three-stage scale – an official water shortage, but not yet a crisis. The Rhine has been running lower than at any point since 1947, leaving cargo barges part-loaded and forcing ferries and river cruises to be cancelled.

Transport ministry water experts have said the period of low river flows could last into December.

World.title: Hockey World Cup kicks off in Amstelveen with Dutch victory
World.content:
The hockey World Cup has begun, with the Dutch women beating Chile 2-0 in the Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen.

Sixteen men’s and 16 women’s teams are competing for the two world titles over the next fortnight. The Netherlands is co-hosting with Belgium, where matches are at the new Belfius Hockey Arena in Wavre, south-east of Brussels.

Both Dutch teams play all five of their group matches at the Wagener Stadium.

The Dutch women

The women’s team is the clear favourite. It holds the world, Olympic and European titles and tops the world rankings by a wide margin.

The tournament is the last of Xan de Waard’s career. The 30-year-old midfielder, twice named the world’s best player, announced in the spring that she would retire afterwards.

De Waard has won all three World Cups she has played in, in 2014, 2018 and 2022. According to NOS, no hockey player, male or female, has won four.

“I think we are always the favourites, so we are now as well,” she told the broadcaster.

The Dutch men

The men are Olympic champions but have not won a world title since 1998. They are ranked second in the world behind Belgium.

Their first match is against New Zealand on Sunday at 4pm, and they play Argentina two days later. Prime minister Rob Jetten is due to attend the tournament as a spectator. His partner, Nicolás Keenan, plays for Argentina and for Klein Zwitserland in The Hague.

Where to watch

NOS is showing all the Dutch matches live on NPO 1, on its website and in its app. Tickets are still on sale through the tournament website, including day tickets covering every match at one venue.

The women’s final is at the Wagener Stadium on August 29 and the men’s final is in Wavre the next day.

World.title: Jetten condemns Star of David stickers at farmers’ protest
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has branded it “a disgusting act” that campaign group Farmers Defence Force (FDF) handed out Star of David stickers at Friday’s farmers’ protest in Den Bosch, according to Omroep Brabant.

The stickers show a Star of David in the pattern of a red farmers’ handkerchief, with the letter B for “boer”, or farmer. The star was a reference to the badge Jews were forced to wear under Nazi occupation.

“If you think you can make your point with this, I think you are only damaging your own cause,” Jetten said.

FDF leader Mark van den Oever said the stickers were meant to underline the injustice being done to farmers. Asked whether he thought the comparison with Jews during the WWII was inappropriate, he said revoking permits was also inappropriate.

Van den Oever also told Hart van Nederland permits were revoked in 1938 and that the same was now being done to farmers, that he understood the stickers could hurt people, but that action groups need to cause friction.

CIDI, a Jewish organisation called the comparison baseless and reprehensible. Ronny Naftaniel, a former director of CIDI and former chairman of the Central Jewish Council, said the farmers were undermining their own position by using the symbol.

Farm permits

The protest was called against the provincial executive’s plan to revoke the nature permits of five poultry farms near protected nature areas, which the farmers say would put them out of business.

After a debate lasting most of Friday, the executive said it was provisionally sticking to that plan, and a no-confidence motion against the executive member responsible, Saskia Boelema, was defeated.

Boelema told the council she had sought contact with the five farmers, who had waited eight months for a response to their plans. Broadcaster NOS, which has seen the email she sent to one of them, reported that it was sent two days before the debate.

The only motion to pass tells the executive to meet the farmers as soon as possible and to consider alternatives such as keeping fewer animals or relocating. A formal decision is due on October 1. Two people died on Friday morning in a crash on the A59, at the back of a queue that had built up as tractors drove to the protest.

World.title: Shell and Philips hit by Russian ransomware attack
World.content:
The Russia-linked ransomware group Cl0p claims to have hacked global corporations Shell and Philips. The two are among nearly 50 companies Cl0p has listed on its website, alongside General Electric and payments firm Fiserv.

From the oil giant, the group says it has taken some 89 gigabytes of material, including technical drawings, facility images, scans of test reports and project plans. They claimed to have stolen another 13.5 gigabytes from health technology company Philips, mostly diagrams and blueprints.

Both companies are investigating, with Shell saying it is “aware of a possible incident”.

Philips said it had “identified and contained an attempted cybersecurity compromise of a specific enterprise server related to internal data”. A spokesperson told NOS that the incident is now under control and has no impact on its customers.

Russian hackers

Cl0p, which has been active since 2019, is a Russia-linked ransomware group that has likely already extorted $500 million from other victims.

It operates by stealing files and other sensitive data from companies and then threatens to publish them online unless a ransom is paid.

There’s no word yet on how much money the hackers are asking for in exchange for not selling or releasing the stolen data.

Security researchers have linked the campaign to a flaw in Windchill, engineering software made by American firm PTC, which was patched on June 17. Neither Shell nor Philips has said how it was breached.

Writing about the attacks, TNW editor-in-chief Ana-Maria Stanciuc said the pattern carried an uncomfortable lesson: “When enough of the corporate world standardises on the same enterprise platform, one shared supplier quietly becomes everyone’s single point of failure, and no amount of internal security spending can fully patch a hole in someone else’s code.”

World.title: Jetten tells farmers to get off motorways after two die in crash
World.content:
Prime minister Rob Jetten has said it is “unacceptable” that tractors were driving on the A59 motorway on Friday, after two people were killed and six injured in a crash. The collision happened at the back of a queue that had built up as the tractors drove to a protest in Den Bosch.

“It is unacceptable and incomprehensible to demonstrate on the motorway because it leads to very dangerous situations,” Jetten said during a press conference.

Jetten also said the decision not to stop the tractors earlier was not a good signal and would have to be reviewed. News agency ANP reported that 50 tractors were driving on the A2 towards Utrecht as he spoke. “Don’t do it, get off the motorway,” Jetten said.

Police said four cars were involved and that they were still investigating what caused the collision, but no tractors were involved.

The victims have not been identified. The tractors had been in the right-hand lane and other traffic could pass on the left, but a traffic jam still built up.

Disputed agreements

Tractors are not permitted on Dutch motorways. Earlier this week the public prosecution department (OM) and the police said they would not stop farmers who drove onto them, citing the right to demonstrate.

A spokesperson for the OM in Oost-Brabant told broadcaster NOS that this had not been agreed. The authorities help demonstrations go ahead, the spokesperson said, but once a tractor is on the motorway it is up to the local mayor, police and prosecutors to decide when and how to step in.

“A tractor on the motorway is never allowed, and is a criminal offence” the spokesperson said. The OM did not answer questions from NOS about what had been agreed instead, or why nobody intervened.

Provincial council members held a minute’s silence for the two dead. Mark van den Oever of Farmers Defence Force called on farmers at the provincial offices not to travel home by motorway.

What the protest is about

Noord-Brabant’s provincial executive intends to revoke the nature permits of five poultry farms close to protected nature areas, after environmental groups won a court case in April 2025.

The court found the protected areas were overloaded with nitrogen, and that the farms were a significant cause. But it stopped short of ordering the permits withdrawn, giving the province, the farmers and the environmental groups a year to come up with a plan that would cut nitrogen levels for good.

The farmers sent in their plans in November 2025 but in July were told their permits would be revoked, although that decision is not yet final. The provincial executive has admitted it never gave them a proper response to those plans, Omroep Brabant reported.

Members of the provincial council, which oversees the executive, broke off their summer break on Friday for a debate on the plan demanded by seven opposition parties, led by farmers’ party BBB. Saskia Boelema, the executive member responsible, told them the province should have sat down with the farmers earlier and apologised for the way the process had been handled.

World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among the thousands to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. The proportion of children taking Catholic catechism in schools has continued to fall but remains a majority https://t.co/5bu35hzJ7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.title: Poland seeks to boost investment with new tax-free personal accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and who Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has only a majority of nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. It also saw its highest-ever proportion of revenue from foreign markets https://t.co/uhGWJVQvf3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 7, 2026 On Thursday, Tusk claimed that the re-introduced CPN would lead to Poland having among “the lowest prices in Europe”, helping “possibly millions of Polish drivers, on critical days, when they return from holidays”. But he also acknowledged that fuel would “still be expensive”. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained a Russian national who it says was planning to assassinate a person with joint US and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. The news was first announced by Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a press conference on Thursday afternoon. “Thanks to the truly brilliant action of our security services – the Internal Security Agency (ABW) with the assistance of the police – on 7 August we detained a Russian citizen, recruited by Russian intelligence services, whose task was to execute an American and Ukrainian citizen right here in Warsaw,” he said. “This is the first time someone on Russian orders has decided to attack an American citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” added Tusk. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: 7 sierpnia zatrzymaliśmy obywatela Rosji, którego zadaniem było wykonanie egzekucji w Warszawie na obywatelu amerykańskim i ukraińskim równocześnie. Dzięki akcji ABW i Policji udało się temu zapobiec. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Though the prime minister said he was not allowed to name either the suspect or the target, he revealed that the latter was someone who is “inconvenient for Putin’s regime”. Tusk also gave no details of how the assassination was supposed to have been carried out, but said that it was foiled “at the last minute”. In a subsequent statement, Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of Poland’s security services, confirmed Tusk’s announcement and noted that the operation to prevent the attack had taken place in cooperation with the US. Police headquarters in Warsaw later revealed that the 29-year-old suspect had been charged with planning a murder and accepting an order to carry out murder in return for material or personal benefit. Both crimes carry jail terms of between two and 15 years. He has also been placed in court-approved pretrial detention. 7 sierpnia br. ABW we współpracy z policją zatrzymała obywatela Rosji, który na zlecenie obcej służby przygotowywał zabójstwo obywatela USA ukraińskiego pochodzenia. Do zabójstwa miało dojść w Warszawie. Operacja była realizowana we współpracy ze służbami USA. — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) August 13, 2026 Poland has been a major target for hostile operations by agents working on behalf of Russia. In February, a report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism found that Poland is the most frequently targeted country in a campaign of sabotage being orchestrated by Russia across Europe. That included an attempt last year to use explosives to derail a train. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland. Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer, who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace. Poland has also been one of Ukraine’s closest allies since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, providing significant military, humanitarian and diplomatic support, as well as welcoming millions of Ukrainian refugees, almost one million of whom remain in Poland. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society.
